paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: this whole chapter is about where you run and what you let out of your mouth. Proverbs 18:10 says, "The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run to it and are safe." A rich man's wealth, though, is only "like a high wall in his imagination" (Proverbs 18:11). One of those walls holds up when the heat comes, and the other one melts like a fortress made of cookie dough.

Then the chapter keeps coming back to the tongue, and it does NOT let up. A fool's mouth is his ruin (Proverbs 18:7), a man who answers before he hears is showing folly (Proverbs 18:13), and "Life and death are in the power of the tongue" (Proverbs 18:21). I think that means every word you say is a seed, and you will eat what grows. So listen first, friend, and ask yourself what you are planting before it leaves your mouth.

And one more thing, because this chapter starts with a man who isolates himself and ends with a friend. Proverbs 18:24 says there is "a friend who stays closer than a brother." You were never made to wall yourself up alone and chase your own way. Run to the LORD, stay humble, and keep the kind of friends who stick, and you will be standing in the right place when the heat comes.
